title: Moore v. Moore (1978)
summary: Trial of child-related issues supported conforming the pleadings, while financial evidence alone did not establish consent to litigate spousal support.
notes: Father Reuben Moore filed the custody action; after trial the court orally awarded custody and child support to the mother (with visitation conditioned on a $7,500 bond) and let her file a post-trial counterclaim conforming to the evidence. The D.C. Court of Appeals held custody, child support and attorney's fees were tried by implied consent, but separate maintenance was not because the father lacked notice and an opportunity to contest it.

sections.Parties: The parents disputed custody and related relief in a domestic-relations proceeding.
sections.Material Facts: The proceeding developed evidence about the child’s welfare and the parents’ financial circumstances. Relief concerning support for the child and arrangements surrounding custody was intertwined with what the parties actually litigated. A claim for spousal support raised a separate issue, although some of the same financial evidence could be relevant to it.
sections.Procedural History: The appellate court considered whether the relief exceeded the pleadings and whether the issues had been tried by consent.
sections.Issue: Which unpleaded issues could be treated as part of the case because the parties actually tried them?
sections.Holding: Child-related relief could follow the issues litigated, but spousal support was not established as an issue tried by consent merely by the admission of financial evidence.
sections.Reasoning: The rule allowing pleadings to conform to trial recognizes that litigation may develop beyond the original documents. Its safeguard is actual express or implied consent to trying the additional issue. When evidence already has a legitimate role in an existing issue, admitting it does not necessarily notify an opponent that a new claim is also being tried. The court therefore distinguished the child-related questions from an additional spousal-support claim.

learning.why: Trial of child-related issues supported conforming the pleadings, while financial evidence alone did not establish consent to litigate spousal support.

topics.cp-trial-consent: Issues actually tried by consent could support relief beyond the original pleadings.
topics.cp-amendment: Evidence relevant to an already pleaded issue did not automatically establish consent to try another.
topics.cp-frcp-15: The decision applies Rule 15(b)'s implied-consent standard to post-trial amendment of pleadings.

mnemonic.rationale: A custody fight and a late counterclaim
